faq.q: What gas comes out when baking soda meets vinegar?
faq.a: Carbon dioxide, the same gas that makes fizzy drinks fizzy and that we breathe out.
asks: What are the bubbles in a vinegar volcano?

faq.q: Is baking soda an acid or a base?
faq.a: Baking soda is a mild base. Dissolved in water it has a pH of about 8 to 9, and it reacts with acids like vinegar or lemon juice.
The reaction uses up the ingredients. Once all the acid or all the baking soda has reacted, no more gas is made.
asks: Why does the volcano stop erupting?

faq.q: Why does the mixture feel cold?
faq.a: This reaction takes in a little heat from its surroundings, so the mixture gets slightly colder. Reactions that do this are called endothermic.
asks: Does baking soda and vinegar get cold?

faq.q: How is a vinegar volcano like a real volcano?
faq.a: Only in how it looks. A real volcano erupts molten rock pushed by gas from deep underground; the model just shows gas bubbling out of a liquid.
asks: Is a baking soda volcano like a real one?

facts: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, with the chemical formula NaHCO3.
Household vinegar is usually about 4 to 8 percent acetic acid in water.

quiz.say: What are the bubbles in the baking soda and vinegar reaction?
quiz.show: What are the bubbles in the baking soda and vinegar reaction?
quiz.why: The acid and base make carbonic acid, which breaks down into water and carbon dioxide gas.

wrong.1: No oxygen is released in this reaction.
wrong.2: The mixture does not get hot enough to make steam; in fact it cools a little.
